findingsCorrected.finding: The package correctly explained --release but assumed its use and did not direct inspection of source/target builds' effective platform classes. A class-file major number could be mistaken for an API compatibility guarantee.
findingsCorrected.evidence: Temurin javac25 -source17 -target17 accepted a call to List.getFirst, emitted major61 and the artifact passed on JVM25. The same source failed under --release17 and passed under --release21. Oracle documents platform-class selection separately and List.getFirst since21.
findingsCorrected.consequence: A toolchain upgrade can silently link a newer platform API while retaining an older class-file target; JVM25 test success does not justify a Java17 consumer claim.
findingsCorrected.correction: Distinguish all five compilation/runtime dimensions, inspect actual consumer minimum and platform API selection, preserve matching source/target plus platform classes when justified, and bound runtime evidence. Added conditional Java17 versus Java21 decision without changing any consumer baseline.
findingsCorrected.supportedAlternative: If consumers already require21, getFirst is available; no API rewrite follows merely from historical source/target17 settings. --release21 is one way to enforce that existing minimum.
findingsCorrected.claimLimit: The focused technical fixture confirms compiler/platform behavior and exception preservation. No Java17/21 VM was run.
